title: Unresolved loci and codimension-stratum geometry
statement:
For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], write $c_X(x)=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ using ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Its singular set is $\operatorname{Sing}(X)=\{x:\mathcal O_{X,x}\text{ is not regular local}\}$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For any subset $Z\subseteq X$ and $r\in\mathbf N$, put $Z^{(r)}=\{x\in Z:c_X(x)=r\}$, and let $\operatorname{Gen}(Z)$ be the ambient images of the generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the subspace $Z$. Write $\overline Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ for the reduced induced closed subscheme of $\overline Z$, expressed by its radical vanishing ideal sheaf [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

For a finite ordinary blowup tower $A$ on $X$ [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], define $T(A)$ to be the union of the image of $\operatorname{Sing}(A_n)$ and the images of the singular sets of every scheme-theoretic center $V_i$, under their structural maps to $X$. A subset $D\subseteq X$ has pure ambient codimension $e$ if $c_X(s)=e$ for every $s\in\operatorname{Gen}(D)$. For a scheme morphism $f:W\to X$, say that $W$ is schematically dense over its generic image points if for every open $U\subseteq W$ and $a,b\in\mathcal O_W(U)$, equality of their germs at every $w\in U$ satisfying $f(w)\in\operatorname{Gen}(f(W))$ implies $a=b$. This expresses that functions are determined on the local schemes over the generic image points; when the image is closed these are exactly the local-scheme restrictions in Temkin's admissibility definition.

source.place: Temkin arXiv:0904.1592v2, §§2.1.6--2.1.7 (schematic density and admissibility), 2.1.9 (singular locus), 4.1.1--4.1.3 (unresolved loci and equicodimension), and §4.3 (lowest codimension strata); Stacks 01J3 for the reduced closed structure.
